doc.title: Frank Foster and Bill Hughes interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Schenectady, New York, March 28, 1995

chapter: Jazz today and writing for Joe Williams
title: Bands carrying on tradition today
summary: Foster names young small groups, repertory orchestras and big bands that keep the tradition alive.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: That leads to another thought is the fact that the Basie band had a very distinct, the whole band had a very personal sound.
Definitely.

I want to ask you, what groups do you see existing today, if there are any, that approximate that kind of personal sound that you’ve come to like and enjoy in the Basie band. Are there any groups or specific artists that you think are perpetuating what jazz is really about today?
Certainly.
Could you name a couple of those groups?

Young groups, you know like Terrance Blanchard, of course the Elvin Jones group makes use of a lot of youngsters such as Nicholas Payton and they even use Coltrane’s son, Ravi Coltrane with Elvin Jones. And of course Vincent Herring, an alto saxophonist, Jesse Davis, another alto saxophonist, Bobby Watson, another alto saxophonist, Roy Hargrove, Chris McBride, Antonio Hart. These are the youngsters that are, that are carrying on authentic jazz. This is not the Basie style, now, I’m talking about small group jazz. And there are, there are many others that doing it. The Harper Brothers, they broke up as a group, but the two of them are doing like straight ahead jazz. And if you’re speaking of big bands that have distinctive sounds, there are a few of those around, but your question wasn’t relating to other bands doing the Basie thing.
No, not necessarily doing the Basie thing, but in other words, just putting your thumb on the pulse and saying, are the traditions alive and well?

Yeah, I would say the traditions are alive and well. Illinois Jacquet has a band that’s a very good band, and of course he’s from the old school, and the arrangements are from that same school. And a lot of the guys are in that generation, mixed with younger guys, really doing very well. And there are some bands around New York, well I don’t know how you rate Toshiko Akiyoshi, but as far as I’m concerned she’s an excellent writer and she gets a lot of great sounds, chords and textures out of that band. Then the GRP All Star Band has got a wonderful sound.
How often does that band play though?
I don’t know, I don’t know.
If they’re all together—
Yeah, I think they just get together and record, and then that’s the last you see of them. I don’t know if they make in person —
Yeah, I think most of those guys have individual careers that they’re pursuing, you know.

Then you have the Carnegie Hall band under the direction of Jon Faddis, the Lincoln Center Orchestra under the direction of Wynton Marsalis, these are perpetuating different © Fillius Jazz Archive -13-
styles, like from Jelly Roll Morton to Louis Armstrong to Fats Waller to Duke Ellington, etcetera, etcetera, Basie, and they’re sort of repertory orchestras.
I think the Smithsonian has one as well.
Smithsonian, yes, with Doug Harris, which we just saw him, not Doug Harris, Doug Richards, why do I say Doug Harris? Doug Richards, from VCU, down at the Smithsonian. Wonderful job.
What do they call that band that he puts together?
I’m not sure of the name of it.
They do a lot of old, you know—
Yeah, yeah, the traditional.
I understand he has an insight to a lot of the original charts because they were at the
Yes, he does. He’s the right person for that job. He does a wonderful job with that.
So it’s going on. You know it’s still going on.
Some bands around New York, you know Maria Schneider is a lady who has a kicking band and she does some wonderful writing.
Is that, that’s not Diva?
No I don’t think that’s Diva, that’s another.
Yeah, that’s an all girl, all woman, that’s another.
Doesn’t John LaBarbara write for them?
He may, I haven’t heard that name.
I think so, yeah.
